_comment: How hard the fight is, chosen once per run beside the class.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A SETTINGS ROW. scenes/options.py is
drawn on the line that nothing on it may change how a fight resolves --
'a difficulty row would be a balance decision worn as a preference, and
the project's whole measurement culture rests on balance decisions being
made in data/ where they can be swept'. That refusal is still correct and
still stands. This is the other half of the same sentence: the decision
lives here, in content, with a sweep axis behind it.
WHAT A TIER MOVES, AND THE DECISION THIS REVERSES. It used to be one
dial: 'incoming', the multiplier on damage arriving at the hero, and this
comment used to argue at length that nothing else should move -- 'not
enemy health, not cadence, not counts' -- on the grounds that enemy
time-to-kill is the number the whole cadence layer is tuned against, and
moving it with a menu moves the thing every stage was tuned against.
That argument was not wrong and it has been overruled on purpose. A tier
is now a statement about the monsters as well as about the cost of a
mistake: 'enemies' below carries six per-mille dials, and the harder
tiers field creatures that notice you sooner, arrive faster, take an
extra hit and shrug some of yours off entirely.
The half of the old argument that still protects the project is kept, and
it is the important half: NORMAL IS STILL BIT-IDENTICAL. Every dial's
identity is its declared default, Difficulty.is_identity checks all of
them, and Table.load still refuses a default tier that is not the
identity. So the recorded 280-cell grid is provably unmoved and only the
other three tiers are new territory.
READING THE DIALS. hp/damage/speed/aggro are per-mille multipliers whose
identity is 1000. 'cadence' scales the pause between attacks, so BELOW
1000 IS MORE OFTEN. 'evasion' is an additive per-mille chance to avoid a
hit outright and ITS IDENTITY IS 0, not 1000 -- it is the odd one out and
it is the one to check first when a tier does not feel the way it reads.
THREE THINGS ON THE RECORD ABOUT THESE LEVERS.
* hp is the strongest lever for an ordinary creature (revenant 46->32
was the single biggest move in acts V-VIII) and nearly INERT on a
boss, whose enrage threshold is a fraction -- it spends the same
proportion of a shorter fight enraged. One percentage, two effects.
* cadence is a WEAK lever. A flanker pause taken 20->38, most of the way
to a charger's, moved not one seed of eight on three separate stages.
* aggro is aimed at disengaging, which the reaction ladder says is the
thing that actually separates a won run from a lost one. Probably the
strongest dial here and certainly the least measured.
MEASURED 2026-08-22, AND IT COST THE FIRST DRAFT. Knight, 8 seeds, all
twenty stages. THE DIALS COMPOUND MUCH HARDER THAN THEY READ. The first
draft of nightmare (incoming 1600, hp 1300, damage 1100, aggro 1300,
cadence 700, evasion 120) left 15 of 20 stages unclearable from FULL
HEALTH, three of them 0/8, with the run ending on stage 3 -- not a hard
tier, a broken one. hard was over the line too at incoming 1300 plus
modest monster dials: 5 walls, where the old one-dial Relentless at the
same 1300 cleared 40/40. Six moderate settings multiply into an
impossible one.
So both were pulled back, and the shape of the fix is the point: incoming
came DOWN to make room for the monsters, because the monsters are what a
tier is supposed to be about now. 'damage' was taken out entirely -- it
duplicates incoming and was the cheapest thing to give up. Turn it back
on before raising incoming again, and sweep after every single change.
ROLLBACK: set every tier's 'incoming' to 1000 and delete every 'enemies'
block. Every branch added for this is guarded on the identity, so the
code goes inert and the game is arithmetically today's -- exactly as
loot.json switches off at gold.base 0.
MEASURED: nothing below except 'normal', which is measured by every
recorded number in the project by construction. The other three are
opening bids and are marked as such until tools/balance.py --difficulty
has swept them. What must hold and is checked by the suite: the gentlest
tier still loses every face-tank run. Only the ceiling and there is no
game -- and easy now weakens the monsters as well as the hits, so that
bracket is the one this file is most likely to break.
